claim_decisions.reason: The 70 frozen payload files match the assigned size/SHA identities in two read-only checks. The report, both new programs and actual J row agree on the fixed mean, support, photon-number weights and exact-real semantics. Remote intake was performed by the owner; no fresh remote source fetch is claimed by this reviewer.
PHYS24's reviewed strict convexity, endpoint signs and mean-18 k(m)<0<B(m) are admitted within their fixed-J initial-time scope. This review neither reopens nor reruns PHYS19–24.

Compactness of Borel probability measures on I, continuity of the three moment functionals and the positive endpoint law establish nonempty compact feasibility and attainment. Mixing any strictly positive-response law with delta_m lowers its positive variance until response is zero, so every minimum is active. The maximum feasible variance is (m-a)(b-m).

The finite-dimensional convex-hull representation and mass/mean/response-preserving perturbation reduce a minimum to at most three atoms without claiming every optimizer has that support. The exact dimensionless counterexample has nonnegative dual x^2(1-x^2)/2, zero set {-1,0,1}, and unique weights (1/8,3/4,1/8); it correctly disproves generic two-line optimality from strict convexity alone.

Independent algebraic reading of the original HI fit verifies alpha=-7/2+2/(ya*z^2-1)+p/[2(1+z)]=N/(2G), the shifted heating representation, and the third-derivative numerator T. Differentiating the R representation and the five shifted-log-operator route have correct factors and denominators. The raw certificate contains 18 negative rational Bernstein coefficients on an enclosure of all I, with positive prefactors, inverse-basis identity and 17/17 first checks. This proves k'''<0 conditional on the fixed serialized J.
limits: Exact rational arithmetic is inspectable implementation evidence, not a proof-assistant trust-kernel proof.
No enclosure of upstream J or atomic uncertainty.
The auxiliary z interval uses the smooth algebraic extension; physical application stays on I.

claim_decisions.reason: The anchored response R(v)=((v-m)k(a)+(m-a)k(v))/(v-a) has derivative (m-a)D_v/(v-a)^2 with D_v=integral_a^v (u-a)k''(u)du>0. Its inherited opposite signs at m,b give a unique interior exact root v*. The stated probabilities have mass one and mean m, and variance (m-a)(v*-m).

lambda2=(v-a)^2/D_v>0 and the root equation give the exact tangent-remainder form of h. The integral remainder H_v(E) applies on both sides of v and at v by continuity. k'''<0 makes H_v strictly decreasing on all I, so H_v(E)<=H_v(a)=1/lambda2; h>=0 with zero set exactly {a,v}. This is a continuum certificate, independent of sampled slack checks.

Integrating h against any Borel probability of mean m gives V-Vstar-lambda2*A>=0. Feasibility A>=0 forces V>=Vstar. The root-defined law attains A=0,V=Vstar. Equality then forces A=0 and support on the two residual zeros; mass/mean uniquely fix the law. Continuous, multi-line and alternate two-line measures are covered, with no unproved restriction to an ansatz.

The standalone degree-five log Taylor jet differentiates the original fit and retains the E^-1 conversion terms. The distinct direct-fit FD path uses exact rational 13-node stencils and recorded moments; Richardson factor 256 is correctly limited to the leading h^8 fifth-derivative term. The first execution has 127/127 checks, three 240-iteration roots, declared frozen tolerances and focused comparisons. The recorded kernel, photon-number, mean, variance and contact normalization are consistent.
limits: Decimal root brackets and FD agreement are numerical checks, not rigorous interval or physical-error enclosures.
127 checks are not 127 independent physical results.
Both numerical paths share the original physics and source constants.

They evaluate the exact root-defined solution. The finite midpoint has small negative response and is explicitly not declared exactly feasible; the stored positive endpoint is also explicitly only numerically feasible.

The positive multiplier gives strict negativity for every subcritical law and unique zero response at the threshold. For each supercritical feasible variance W, choosing v=m+W/(m-a) on the anchored family supplies a strictly positive-response law. This is existential, not universal. Strict-positive response requires V>Vstar but anchored laws approach Vstar from above, so the infimum is Vstar and there is no minimizer.

The right-endpoint anchored law at variance Vstar is distinct from Pstar and therefore has strictly negative response by the unique equality case. Continuity gives a nonempty interval immediately above Vstar with negative right-anchored response while the left-anchored law is positive at the same mean and variance. The report correctly leaves the far boundary and full variance-response envelope unresolved.
The viewed figure depicts the numerical two-line law and contact residual consistently and includes the conditional scope. It contributes no independent proof of a continuous inequality.
